config.title: Crypto module

intro.title: Crypto module
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple password hashing and verification tool using Node.js's built-in Crypto module. You will learn how to use cryptographic functions to securely hash passwords with a salt and later verify them against stored hashes. The core programming concepts involve working with asynchronous functions, buffers, and string encoding. You'll primarily use the crypto.pbkdf2Sync method and handle hex encoding to create and compare hashes. This hands-on project will give you practical experience with essential security practices in Node.js applications.
intro.usecase: The Crypto module is essential for building secure applications that handle sensitive data. You'll use it to hash passwords before storing them in databases, create digital signatures for API authentication, and encrypt sensitive user information like payment details. In e-commerce platforms, it secures transaction data; in banking apps, it protects account information; and in authentication systems, it ensures passwords remain confidential even if databases are compromised. Every time you log into a website or make an online purchase, cryptographic operations are working behind the scenes to keep your data safe.

objectives: Initialize the crypto module in a Node.js application
Construct hash values using different cryptographic algorithms
Implement password hashing with salt generation
Configure encryption and decryption using symmetric keys
Generate secure random data for cryptographic operations
Manipulate cryptographic keys for digital signatures
Integrate crypto functions into practical Node.js applications

steps.title: Import the crypto module
steps.instruction: Import the crypto module using require('crypto') at the top of your file.
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import Node.js built-in modules. The crypto module is built into Node.js, so you don't need to install it separately.

steps.title: Create a function to generate random bytes
steps.instruction: Create a function named generateRandomBytes that uses crypto.randomBytes() to generate 16 bytes and returns them as a hex string.
steps.hint: Use the crypto module's randomBytes method to create random bytes, then convert them to a hexadecimal string.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function that generates 16 random bytes and returns them as a hex string.
successCriteria: The generateRandomBytes function is defined, uses crypto.randomBytes(16), and returns the result as a hex string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function returns the bytes as a hex string using .toString('hex').
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've created a function named generateRandomBytes that calls crypto.randomBytes(16) and returns the hex string.

steps.title: Create a function to create a hash
steps.instruction: Create a function called createHash that takes input data and returns a SHA-256 hash as a hex string.
steps.hint: Use crypto.createHash('sha256') to create a hash object, update it with the input data, then call digest('hex') to get the hexadecimal string.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named createHash that accepts input data and returns its SHA-256 hash as a hex string.
successCriteria: The createHash function is defined, uses crypto.createHash('sha256'), updates with input, and returns digest('hex').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function takes input data, creates a SHA-256 hash, updates it, and returns the hex digest.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't quite right. Remember to use crypto.createHash('sha256'), update it with the input, and call digest('hex') to return the hash string.

steps.instruction: Create a function named createHMAC that takes data and a secret key as parameters,
steps.hint: Use crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret) to create an HMAC object, then call .update(data) and .digest('hex') on it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A createHMAC function that returns an HMAC-SHA256 hex string when given data and a secret key.
successCriteria: The createHMAC function is defined, takes data and secret parameters, uses crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret), calls .update(data) and .digest('hex'), and returns the result.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your function takes both data and secret parameters, uses 'sha256' as the algorithm, and returns the hex digest.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't quite right. Make sure you're using crypto.createHmac() with 'sha256', passing the secret, updating with data, and digesting as hex.

steps.title: Create a function for password hashing with scrypt
steps.instruction: Create a function named hashPassword that takes a password parameter and returns a promise that resolves to a hex string hash using crypto.scrypt() with a salt length of 16.
steps.hint: Use crypto.scrypt() which returns a promise. Generate a random salt with crypto.randomBytes(16) and use it with the password. The promise resolves with a Buffer that you can convert to hex.
steps.expectedOutcome: A hashPassword function that returns a promise for secure password hashing using scrypt.
successCriteria: The hashPassword function is defined, takes a password parameter, uses crypto.scrypt() with a 16-byte salt, and returns a promise that resolves to a hex string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function returns a promise and uses a 16-byte salt with crypto.scrypt.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or doesn't match the requirements. It should be named hashPassword, take a password, use crypto.scrypt with a salt, and return a promise.

steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an async 'main' function defined that you can later use to call and log results from your crypto functions.
successCriteria: An async function named 'main' is created with proper function syntax.
